walkthrough.content:
QA repair for task 7fe1005f on `main`, building on round 1 (f24c12e, d238d30). At 389px tall with 125% or 150% display scaling there is less than 8rem between the review header and the floating controls, so the sticky rail ran under the mini player. Now `document-review.tsx:298` measures that space (window height divided by the scale, minus the header and the controls' reserved height) and `:1211` switches both rails (`:1311`, `:1350`) to scroll with the page when it is under 8rem. The page already ends past the controls, and the rail controls keep a scroll margin the height of the header. `verify-floating-controls.mjs:46-47` adds the two windows; `:293` and `:306` check the rail mode and that the scrolling rail's end clears the controls. The unit test (`floating-controls.test.ts:112-115`) and the README cover the new behaviour. Commands: `NEXUS_QA_ONLY='screenshot-height' node scripts/document-review-qa/verify-floating-controls.mjs` (before the fix exit 1, 15 FAIL; after the fix PASS); `node scripts/document-review-qa/verify-floating-controls.mjs` (PASS, 308 OK); `node scripts/document-review-qa/verify-drafts.mjs` (PASS); `cd dashboard && npm test` (1008/1017, the 9 failures are the known voice-command-bar ones); `dashboard/node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p dashboard` (clean). Commits: f24c12e, d238d30 (round 1) and 7686e3e (this repair), all local and not pushed. Caveats: the dirty `.env.example` was left untouched and unstaged. At short scaled windows the outline rail no longer stays pinned while scrolling, which is intended. The audio-navigation check failed once in the reproduction run and passed in both runs after the fix; I believe that was a timing glitch in the check.

Quality gates: verify + code-review declared — verify=pass (verify-floating-controls 308 OK exit 0, verify-drafts pass, tsc clean, dashboard tests 1008/1017 with only the 9 known failures, encoding clean); code-review=pass (self-review of the diff: the change only affects the desktop rails, and the mode is recalculated on window resize, display-scale changes and changes to the floating controls)

Criteria attestation (implementer-declared): 4/4 met.
- 1 met — settled in round 1 (f24c12e, d238d30) and not reopened; the full matrix's sticky-mode rail checks still pass in all 9 sticky windows.
- 2 met — with the audio, voice and feedback controls on screen, Finish review, Send to Praxis (hit-tested only) and Keep reviewing are fully visible, on top and working at 1209×389 at 125% and 1600×389 at 150% (exit 0, previously 15 FAILs), and at every desktop, short and phone window (308 checks OK).
- 3 met — real hit-target checks, `verify-drafts.mjs` passes, the audio-across-navigation check passes, and the unit tests are 1008 of 1017 with only the 9 known voice-command-bar failures.
- 4 met — the run's own check confirms the review stayed a draft, the receiver got 0 turns, and there were no finish, submit, approval or decision writes. Everything ran on a throwaway database with a local stand-in receiver.

Workspace binding — home root `/Volumes/Projects/TheNexus` (audit mode: writes into other repos are RECORDED, not refused).
- ✅ every recorded write stayed inside the home root — no additional repo was touched.

walkthrough.content:
# Vault watcher: budgeted, priority-ordered MEMORY.md + supersession

## The defect
`services/vault-watcher/index.js` `regenerateMemoryIndex()` emitted every memory in one `listMarkdown().sort()` alphabetical run with no budget enforcement, while Claude Code injects only the first **200 lines / 25,000 bytes** of `MEMORY.md`. The live file was **227 lines / 23,760 bytes**, so `reference_*` (lines 190–222) lost 22 of its 33 entries past the ceiling and the `projects/ workflows/ incidents/ skills/` pointers (lines 224–227) were invisible entirely — including `reference_vault_hybrid_search`, the doc explaining how to search the vault.

## Files touched (all in /Volumes/Projects/TheNexus)
- `services/vault-watcher/index.js` — modified (+~460/−106 vs QA baseline `494dbb6109cb`)
- `services/vault-watcher/__tests__/memory-index.test.js` — **new**, 24 tests
- `services/vault-watcher/__tests__/dated-series.test.js` — modified (33 lines: re-pointed at the surviving renderer)

## PART 1 — ordering by value
New `buildMemoryIndexLines()` emits, under `##` headings: `reference_` → `feedback_` → `project_` → *other standing prefixes* → directory pointers → `note_` (newest first). Live section map:
```
3:## memories/reference   37:## memories/feedback   74:## memories/project
90:## directories         95:## memories/note — dated notes, newest first
```
An entry matching none of the known prefixes lands in "other standing entries" rather than silently disappearing.

## PART 2 — hard budget
`withinMemoryBudget()` asserts lines ≤ 200 **and** bytes ≤ 25,000 before `writeIfChanged`. Over budget, only the dated-note section degrades, down `NOTE_STAGES = ['series','month','quarter','pointer']` (per-stem-month lines for real series, a pooled `N one-off dated notes in <bucket>` line for one-off stems, then per-quarter, then a single searchable pointer). The existing `SERIES_MIN_MEMBERS=3` collapse is preserved as the top rung. If even the pointer rung will not fit, note lines are dropped from the tail with a marker line and a loud `log()` warning — a `reference_`/`feedback_`/`project_` line is never dropped.

**One judgment call beyond the literal brief, flagged for the reviewer:** the ladder alone landed at 123/200 lines, i.e. 77 lines of budget left empty while 106 individual note lines had been collapsed. So after a rung fits, `promoteNewest` lifts the newest dated notes back onto their own lines one at a time, keeping the last arrangement that still fits (`buildNoteLines(section, entries, stage, promoteNewest)`). The ladder is unchanged and the budget guarantee is unchanged — only leftover budget is spent, on recency. This is why the live file lands on exactly 200 lines rather than 123.

## PART 3 — supersession
`readSupersession(raw)` parses `status: superseded` and `superseded_by:` (either alone is sufficient, so a writer that sets only one still gets the exclusion) and counts `supersedes:` in inline `[a, b]`, block `- a`, and scalar forms, stripping quotes and `[[wiki brackets]]`. Superseded files are excluded from `MEMORY.md` (`collectMemoryEntries`) **and** from the `.index/vault-search.json` chunks (`buildSearchIndexPayload`). A superseding file's line reads `(supersedes N)`.

**Field names verified, not assumed:** I read Praxis task `e524649b-4ed2-4c7a-be13-09563b226f44` through the read-only tool bridge (`nexus_tasks` get). Its PART 3 reads: "Adopt frontmatter `supersedes: [name]` and `status: superseded` + `superseded_by: name`", and its acceptance criterion: "supersedes / status: superseded / superseded_by frontmatter is written by the vault write paths and agreed with sr-g." My implementation uses exactly these three, and the code comment block cites that task ID so the contract is discoverable from the code.

## Code-review finding I fixed in my own diff
Rerouting the memories section through `buildMemoryIndexLines` left `pushSectionEntries()` with **no production caller** — dead code exercised only by its own test file. I deleted it, folded its `SERIES_RECENT_KEPT` guard into `buildNoteLines`'s `series` rung, and re-pointed `dated-series.test.js`'s `render()` helper at `buildNoteLines(..., 'series')`. Two order-sensitive assertions there were updated (sub-threshold dated files, and "preserves alphabetical placement") because dated entries are now newest-first rather than alphabetical — that reordering *is* the deliverable, and the change is commented in the test. All other series-collapse coverage is intact. Separately, `MEMORY_GROUPS` was exported without a consumer; it is now asserted in the ordering test.

## Verification (commands + output)
```
$ node services/vault-watcher/index.js --once
Regenerated projections (once); MEMORY.md 200 lines / 19717 bytes (notes: month),
123 active skills indexed, ... search index 585 docs / 2574 chunks, 0 superseded docs excluded

$ wc -l /Volumes/Projects/shared-mind/MEMORY.md   →  200
$ wc -c /Volumes/Projects/shared-mind/MEMORY.md   →  19717
reference lines in MEMORY.md: 33 ; reference files in vault: 33 ; last at line: 36
PASS: all 33 reference entries within the loaded head
```
**Live supersession probe** (two files created in the vault, then removed): the `status: superseded` file was absent from `MEMORY.md` and its unique body token absent from `.index/vault-search.json`; its replacement rendered as `- [reference_zz_live_probe](...) (supersedes 1)`; the daemon logged `1 superseded docs excluded`. After removal the log returned to `0 superseded docs excluded` and 200/19717.

**Tests:** `npx jest services/vault-watcher` → **47 passed**. Full `npx jest` → **Test Suites: 2 failed, 49 passed; Tests: 1 failed, 406 passed**. Both failures are pre-existing and outside this diff:
- `server/__tests__/openrouter-free-lane.test.js` — a real `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the machine env (known, long-standing).
- `services/vault-watcher/__tests__/collect-skills.test.js` — a `node:test` file jest's `testMatch` picks up but cannot parse ("must contain at least one test"). It existed at the QA baseline (`git show 494dbb6109cb:...` succeeds) and passes **3/3** under `node --test services/vault-watcher/__tests__/collect-skills.test.js`.

**Encoding gate:** strict UTF-8 decode + mojibake scan clean on all four edited text files (`index.js`, both test files, generated `MEMORY.md`).

## Caveats and declarations
- **Daemon restarted.** `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.thenexus.vault-watcher`. Necessary: the long-lived launchd daemon held the old code in memory and would have overwritten the regenerated `MEMORY.md` on the next vault change. It now runs the final code and reproduces 200 lines / 19717 bytes on startup; stderr clean.
- **Additional repo touched: `/Volumes/Projects/shared-mind`** (declared per BC-WORKSPACE-BINDING). Why: the task requires regenerating the live index, which is that repo's generated output. I wrote only watcher-generated projections plus two temporary probe files. The watcher's own hourly git-sync fired mid-probe and auto-committed them (`e530ad9`); I removed the files and ran the watcher's own `runGitSync()` to commit the deletion (`a0321a1`). They are absent from HEAD (`git ls-files | grep zz_` → none) and nothing was pushed (next push ~278 min). No hand-crafted git commands were used on that repo.
- **BC-FOREIGN-WORK honoured.** The 5 modified + 12 untracked foreign files present at dispatch were not read-modified, staged, stashed, reverted, or deleted. No `git add -A` / `git commit -a`. Nothing committed in TheNexus (BC-NO-COMMIT); the work is in the working tree for QA's diff.
- **Follow-up (not in scope, not done):** superseded files are still counted in the `LINKS.md` backlink graph — only `MEMORY.md` and the search chunks exclude them, per the task's PART 3 wording. Worth revisiting once the Praxis sr-i task actually writes supersession frontmatter into the vault; today no vault file carries it, which is why the live run reports `0 superseded docs excluded` and the exclusion is proven by the probe and by tests rather than by existing data.

Quality gates: verify + code-review declared — verify=`node services/vault-watcher/index.js --once` + daemon restart → live MEMORY.md 200 lines / 19717 bytes, all 33 reference_ entries at lines 4-36; live supersession probe excluded from MEMORY.md and vault-search.json; `npx jest services/vault-watcher` 47/47 passed; full `npx jest` 406 passed with 2 named pre-existing failures; code-review=found and fixed two issues in my own diff (`pushSectionEntries` left with no production caller after the rewrite — deleted and its tests re-pointed at `buildNoteLines`; `MEMORY_GROUPS` exported without a consumer — now asserted in the ordering test); no debug/TODO/placeholder leftovers; UTF-8 + mojibake scan clean on all 4 edited text files

Workspace binding — home root `/Volumes/Projects/TheNexus` (audit mode: writes into other repos are RECORDED, not refused).
- ✅ every recorded write stayed inside the home root — no additional repo was touched.

Each rule below is BINDING, not advisory, and carries all four fields it needs to stay binding: what must be resolved first, who can waive it, what to do instead, and what happens if you proceed anyway. Read them off this artifact — you are not expected to reconstruct any of it from elsewhere.

Carry them VERBATIM into anything you hand on (walkthrough, follow-up, summary). A constraint decays into a suggestion through five moves, all of which look like good writing: compressing it, absorbing it into a plan step, converging on it as an agreed detail, deferring its ownership to whoever comes next, or citing a past exception as precedent. If you must restate one, restate all four of its fields; if you cannot, quote the block instead of summarizing it.

#### BC-SCOPE — Deliver the outcome this task names ("Present Nexus views on chosen displays from the Windows travel shell") — do not silently narrow, widen, or transform it.
- **Prerequisite (resolve first):** Read the intended outcome and any acceptance criteria on this record before your first edit, and settle what 'done' means while you can still ask.
- **Authority (who may waive it):** Robert. Scope is his call, and the QA reviewer rules on a criterion you can show is defective — neither happens silently, you have to raise it.
- **Fallback (do this instead):** Deliver in full every part that is not blocked, then say explicitly in the walkthrough what you left out and why. Scaling the work down without saying so is not the fallback.
- **Consequence (if you proceed anyway):** A quietly narrowed delivery reads as complete on the board while the outcome is unmet, so the gap surfaces only at review — as a failed round, not a note.

#### BC-WORKSPACE — Do the work inside /Volumes/Projects/TheNexus — QA's primary diff comes from there; any additional repo you touch must be named in your completion report.
- **Prerequisite (resolve first):** The assigned workspace must be the repo that holds the main body of the code this task changes. Check that before your first edit, not after.
- **Authority (who may waive it):** Praxis, via the task re-point endpoint — POST /api/tasks/9cae1b0e-cba3-4580-a83a-1c3222404dbe/workspace with the new path and a reason. Robert, if the re-point is refused.
- **Fallback (do this instead):** If the WHOLE task belongs elsewhere, re-point the task first and then do ALL the work in the new directory; if you only realise at the end, still call the endpoint with "baseline":"head". If the task merely also needs another repo, work there and declare it in your report. If neither is possible, report needs_input.
- **Consequence (if you proceed anyway):** QA builds the authoritative diff from this workspace and the dispatch-time snapshot, plus the diff of every additional repo the run touched and declared. Work done in an undeclared repo that Praxis could not record is invisible to review, and a round with no work in any visible repo fails as an empty diff no matter how correct the change is.

#### BC-DEPENDENCIES — Do not treat this task as unblocked until its declared dependencies are resolved: 6d6e2638-8fc1-46fa-8545-3ad4d5876dc0, be441473-ebd1-4c93-b3a1-9f3e3d3decf4, 91f1f758-4b40-464b-a2a0-29f29de0bf98.
- **Prerequisite (resolve first):** Each of 6d6e2638-8fc1-46fa-8545-3ad4d5876dc0, be441473-ebd1-4c93-b3a1-9f3e3d3decf4, 91f1f758-4b40-464b-a2a0-29f29de0bf98 must be complete (or explicitly waived) before the work this task depends on them for is valid.
- **Authority (who may waive it):** Robert. Praxis's scheduler files dependencies; it does not drop them, and neither does an executor.
- **Fallback (do this instead):** Deliver only the parts that genuinely do not depend on the unresolved item, say in the walkthrough exactly what you left out and why, and report needs_input if nothing is deliverable.
- **Consequence (if you proceed anyway):** Work built on an unmet dependency is rejected at review and re-filed, spending a correction attempt on a rebuild rather than a fix.

#### BC-CRITERIA — Satisfy every acceptance criterion above and cite the command or observation that proves each one.
- **Prerequisite (resolve first):** Each criterion has to be verified against real behavior before you report complete — a criterion you did not run is a criterion you did not meet.

tasks.name: Add collapse/expand pip to Voice/Start Conversation bar
tasks.description:
What: Add a small clickable pip (toggle indicator) to the floating "Voice" and "Start Conversation" bar in the lower-right corner of The Nexus dashboard UI, letting users collapse it to a minimized state and expand it back.
Why: The bar currently stays fully expanded at all times, which can obstruct content in the lower-right of the dashboard; a collapse/expand control gives users control over screen real estate without removing quick access to voice features.
Heads-up: Needs to preserve the bar's existing click targets and functionality when expanded, and the collapsed state should remain easily discoverable (not fully hidden) so users don't lose track of it.

walkthrough.content:
Added a collapse/expand pip to the global voice dock (the floating Voice / Start conversation bar, lower right).

What changed and why:
- `dashboard/src/components/global-voice-dock.tsx`: the dock is now a flex row. On the left is a pip button: a `›` chevron with aria-label "Collapse voice controls" when expanded; a cyan `‹ 🎤` button with aria-label "Expand voice controls" when collapsed. It has aria-expanded and aria-controls="global-voice-bar". `VoiceCommandBar` sits in a wrapper (`#global-voice-bar`) that is hidden when collapsed, not unmounted, using invisible, max-w-0, max-h-0, overflow-hidden and opacity-0 with a 200 ms transition. Recording, conversation and wake word are therefore never interrupted by collapsing. The choice persists in localStorage under `nexus.voice.dock.collapsed`, read after mount so server and client render the same markup first. Any voice setup request (the "Talk to Praxis" launcher or Alt+Shift+V) expands the dock, because the setup window belongs to the bar and would otherwise be invisible.
- `dashboard/src/lib/__tests__/voice-dock.test.ts`: two new tests. (1) Collapsing hides the bar while keeping the same control elements loaded and saves "1"; expanding restores it and saves "0"; Start conversation and Voice then still start recording. (2) A saved collapsed state is restored on load, and a voice setup request expands the dock and shows the "Talk to Praxis setup" window.

- dashboard/src/components/global-voice-dock.tsx
- dashboard/src/lib/__tests__/voice-dock.test.ts

Keep the long source inventory available below/collapsed, not as the main action. Open a polished responsive three-stage guided workflow matching the existing Nexus UI on desktop and phone. **What changed and why**
- **Exact bytes (QA finding 1):**
  - `readDocumentFile` additionally reports `exactHash`, `exactContent` and `exactByteLength` for the bytes on disk. The existing normalizer is unchanged.
  - For a declared deliverable, the revision's `content_hash` is now the SHA-256 of the exact bytes. That identity drives `expected_content_hash`, receipts, decisions and the decision check.
  - A new add-only table `review_document_revision_exact` keeps the exact text only when it differs from the normalized text (a BOM or CR line endings), so `raw_path` serves exactly the registered bytes.
  - Legacy documents that were never declared keep the line-normalized identity and raw output they always had.
- **Producer pair (QA finding 2):**
  - A document takes a declaration's project only together with its task: the same task, or a chat-era document gaining its first task.
  - A re-declaration from another task or project leaves the document's own pair intact and is recorded on its receipt.

walkthrough.content:
Saving Robert's answer to an executor question no longer puts approved work back on a "Proposal contract changed" hold. Real changes to scope, acceptance criteria or workspace still trigger review. A regression test reproduces the Groundrules incident: 6 of its 8 cases failed on the old code and all 8 pass now. Nothing is live yet: the running Nexus API on :4000 needs a restart, which was not done.

Cause: `contract()` in `db/work-admission.js` counted `antigravity_payload.operator_rulings` as part of the task's scope since commit 08b187a. When Praxis appended an answer, the task's fingerprint changed, and the update check reset an approved task to `needs_evidence`. The live database (read-only) shows this for Groundrules task 7bf1a379: `new_work` became a hold at 16:44:11 UTC on 2026-09-29 and was resolved by hand at 16:47:15.

What changed:
- `db/work-admission.js`:
  - Rulings no longer count toward the fingerprint or identity, so adding an answer keeps the decision, the fingerprint and any earlier manual resolution.
  - Each new answer is recorded on the admission record as `operator_answers` (position, SHA-256 of its text, time); the answer text stays on the task for the executor brief and the QA contract.
  - Removing, rewriting or reordering a ruling that is already recorded still triggers a hold, with the reason "Recorded operator rulings were rewritten or removed".
  - Scope, acceptance or workspace edits still hold the task, even in the same update as an answer. An answer never clears an existing hold or duplicate concern.
  - Admission records written before this change are carried over (recorded as `legacy_fingerprint`) only if they exactly match the task under the old rule.
  - Side effects: a retried task creation after an answer returns the same task instead of a conflict, and an answer on one task no longer re-holds a related task whose approval had compared against it.
- `docs/work-admission.md`: one paragraph describing the above.
- `server/__tests__/work-admission-operator-answers.test.js` (new, 216 lines): 8 cases covering the Groundrules reproduction, repeated and duplicate answers, real scope changes, rewritten rulings, existing holds, related tasks and the carry-over of older records.

Praxis compatibility: no Praxis change is needed. `recordOperatorRuling` (`operator-ruling.ts:152-161`) rewrites the full list with the new entry at the end, which the new check treats as an append. The dispatch checks (`antigravity-tools.ts:2011-2016`, `work-admission/service.ts:86-89`) compare the admission decision and fingerprint, and both stay the same after an answer. The answer-delivery behaviour from f983f0e8 and 6d30d9d3 is untouched.

Verification:
- New test on the old code: 6 failed, 2 passed (the 2 were the checks that real scope changes and existing holds still block).
- After the fix: `npx jest server/__tests__/work-admission` passes, 37 tests (1 skipped).
- Full `npx jest`: 107 of 111 suites pass. The 4 failing suites are unrelated: `openrouter-free-lane`, `praxis-stream` and `studio-route` were already failing before this work, and `model-control-route` started failing during the run because another session is editing `server/routes/model-control.js`, which is not in this change.
- The three changed files pass a strict UTF-8 check and a scan for garbled characters.

After a restart, three things to know:
- Any Praxis day-plan slot approved before the restart for a task that already has rulings will be held once with "task scope changed since the plan was prepared".
- An already-resolved task whose closest matches include a task with rulings will be re-held once. Only 3 tasks in the live database have rulings, all completed.
- Nexus still can't tell who sent an update that adds a ruling; Robert's sign-in is checked on the Praxis side. Closing that gap would need Praxis to send its runtime key when it saves an answer, plus a check in Nexus. That's an optional follow-up.

Other repositories: only read Praxis and the live `nexus.db`; nothing outside `/Volumes/Projects/TheNexus` was edited. No commit, service restart or task change was made, and the uncommitted files that were already in the tree were left as they were.

> Implement Robert's requested endpoint checkpoints end-to-end. This is a direct feature request authorizing investigation and implementation, not a problem-council intake or a request to redesign the goals of all projects.
> 
> VERBATIM REQUEST:
> Can you look into our end state process and add the ability to incorporate checkpoints into the end point? So basically end points, you know, the checkpoint is the current end point until that checkpoint is reached and then it moves on to the next checkpoint automatically. It allows us to keep a visual of the long term end goal, but also understanding that there has to be points that we meet before we reach that end point goal. Like, for example, the Praxis endpoint.
> 
> INTENDED BEHAVIOR:
> Each project can retain a visible long-term end goal and an ordered set of checkpoints. Exactly one checkpoint is current while unfinished checkpoints remain. Its goal and acceptance criteria are the effective endpoint for planning, knowledge needs, task targeting and verification. Once fresh authoritative evidence verifies that checkpoint, automatically record its completion and move to the next defined checkpoint. Keep the long-term goal visible throughout; do not replace it with each short-term goal or append endless horizon prose. Progression through an adopted checkpoint sequence is authorized by this feature request: do not insert a mandatory new operator approval at every machine-verifiable checkpoint. Manual criteria still need their actual required evidence/acceptance. Task execution and external-action gates remain separate.
> 
> CURRENT CONTEXT (refresh before relying):
> Nexus owns adopted definitions; Praxis owns planning/verification/orchestration; @praxis/contract in nexus-shared is the canonical shared schema. Current EndpointDefinitionSchema has beneficiary/scope/exclusions/resource_budget/review_at/completion_policy/proposed_next but no checkpoints. end_state_criteria is an array of stable-ID criteria and evidence observations. Praxis src/knowledge/project-steward.ts evaluates criteria and required knowledge, writes an assessment guarded by project/endpoint revisions, and currently flags achieved endpoints as ready for review without adopting another endpoint. Keep evidence freshness, unavailable/unknown distinctions, manual/metric criteria, skip detection and guarded writes intact. Existing endpoint-history is history, not an adopted checkpoint plan.
> Praxis example project ID c11f3f92-0645-4746-a7d3-0b0722e5a2d3 currently describes bounded autonomy and measured value, mixing prior achieved horizons and next frontier. It is a motivating example, not authority to invent or mark its business/operational checkpoints achieved.
> 
> SCOPE AND DESIGN:
> Home workspace /Volumes/Projects/TheNexus because this task adds the canonical persistence/API and the project UI. Necessary implementation in /Volumes/Projects/Praxis and /Volumes/Projects/nexus-shared is explicitly in scope; declare all roots in completion so QA sees every diff. The shared contract project's parked board status does not prohibit this required dependency change; do not activate that separate project. Inspect any Cortex proxy and mobile contract mirror touched by this wire format, update necessary pass-through/contract handling if needed, and declare additional roots. Keep orchestration in Praxis, persistence in Nexus, shared fields in the contract; no parallel state store and no generic workflow-engine rewrite.
> 
> Inspect existing project edit/display/API/MCP/bridge paths and planning/council/knowledge consumers, then write a concise in-repo design before implementation. Resolve routine schema/UI choices yourself from Robert's clear behavior request. Support stable checkpoint IDs, ordered definitions, per-checkpoint criteria and linked required knowledge where applicable, status/evidence/history, and unambiguous active checkpoint selection. Distinguish project-wide invariant requirements from current-checkpoint requirements so future work does not block the present checkpoint. Keep prior evidence attached to the exact definition it verified; changed criteria cannot reuse old success as proof.
> 
> Preserve existing projects without checkpoints and existing API clients without silent data loss. Partial legacy writes must not erase checkpoints. Editing a long-term goal, checkpoint sequence or criteria must be guarded against concurrent updates and invalidate only affected current assessments. Archive removed checkpoints/history instead of destroying evidence. Handle add/edit/reorder and invalid selections coherently; no hidden skips or accidental completion from an empty/all-disabled criteria set.
> 
> AUTOMATIC ADVANCEMENT:
> Use a single authoritative, revision-guarded persisted transition. Persist completed-checkpoint evidence and the new current checkpoint together or with equivalent durable atomic semantics. Duplicate callbacks/steward cycles, retries, restarts and concurrent edits cannot skip checkpoints or duplicate completion events. A fresh assessment for the active checkpoint definition is required; failure, unavailable evidence, manual criteria lacking acceptance, skipped/cancelled tasks or unresolved required knowledge must not advance. Do not equate an implementer's exit or generic completed task label with independent review passed; honor current evaluator/QA semantics and preserve degraded evidence. Evaluate a next checkpoint against its own evidence, never inherit the predecessor's pass. Do not regress automatically into an endless oscillating loop; record later regressions visibly and document the policy.
> 
> When the final checkpoint is verified, record the checkpoint sequence as complete and evaluate overall completion according to adopted final-goal criteria/invariants and existing completion policy. Do not generate a new horizon, auto-park/archive the project, or claim a broad business outcome solely because an intermediate milestone is green. A checkpoint transition is not permission to dispatch tasks outside the approved scheduler flow.
> 
> USER EXPERIENCE:
> On project endpoint views and editing surfaces, show long-term goal, current checkpoint, progress through the ordered sequence and upcoming checkpoints. Completed checkpoints expose supporting evidence/date in an understandable history. The current checkpoint needs a prominent 'working toward now' treatment; the big goal remains visible. Support authoring/reordering/editing checkpoints and acceptance criteria through the normal project UI and API/tool route, so the feature is usable beyond a fixture. Clearly distinguish no checkpoints, waiting for evidence, current, completed and an unverified final goal. Keep phone-size dashboard usable and shared state consistent across screens. Update relevant tool schemas/descriptions, briefing/goal-regression/planning and endpoint-interview workflow guidance so Praxis actually works toward the active checkpoint, not the far-future list. Update source docs, not generated AGENTS/skill projections.
> 
> VALIDATION AND EXAMPLE:
> Provide a reviewable proposed Praxis checkpoint sequence grounded in its live recorded endpoint/criteria in a local demo/test fixture or clearly labelled proposal; do not overwrite the adopted Praxis goal or silently invent/adopt thresholds on Robert's behalf. Demonstrate a representative 3-checkpoint project: long-term goal remains constant, first checkpoint passes and advances exactly once, second fails/unavailable and stays current, then verified evidence advances; final completion honors the actual policy. Include meaningful tests for serialization/old clients, duplicate events/restarts/concurrency, stale definition evidence, no criteria/manual criteria, required-knowledge scoping, skipped tasks, final checkpoint semantics, and planning targeting. Run focused contract/API/runtime/UI tests and required build/type checks; verify the actual UI on an isolated test project/server where needed. Do not run side-effecting production probes or mutate real endpoint acceptance data to prove the feature.
> 
> DELIVERY:
> Implement the feature, maintain current foreign work, document architecture/migration and any runtime activation step, and submit both verify/code-review evidence plus normal independent Nexus QA. Check applicable repo instructions. No commits/pushes, public deployment, destructive cleanup, production supervisor restart or unrequested endpoint adoption. If service reload is needed, state exactly what remains; source implemented, QA passed, and running activation are separate claims. Avoid stopping at a proposal or a schema-only/UI-only partial feature.
acceptance_criteria: A persisted ordered checkpoint model keeps the long-term goal independent, with stable IDs, per-checkpoint acceptance evidence and one effective current checkpoint; existing projects and legacy writes preserve data.

Project UI and supported API/MCP/bridge tools allow checkpoints to be authored and viewed, with clear long-term/current/upcoming/completed progress and retained completion evidence on desktop and narrow screens.

Fresh verification of the current checkpoint automatically advances exactly once through a durable guarded transition; failed/unavailable/stale/manual-unaccepted/skipped-task evidence and unresolved applicable needs cannot advance it.

Praxis planning, goal regression, briefing and knowledge/verification consumers target the effective current checkpoint while retaining the long-term goal and appropriately scoping future versus current requirements.

Final-checkpoint handling preserves final-goal criteria and completion policy; duplicate/restarted/concurrent evaluation cannot skip checkpoints or create false completion, and definition edits invalidate affected evidence.
A representative three-checkpoint end-to-end demonstration and focused contract/API/runtime/UI tests pass; a proposed Praxis example is reviewable without modifying its adopted endpoint.

All touched workspaces and activation requirements are declared, relevant endpoint-workflow documentation updated, and normal verify/code-review plus independent Nexus QA cover the complete implementation.

USE CASE / INTENDED OUTCOME
The NexusDashboard on :3000 serves every route at HTTP 200 after a clean `npm install` in TheNexus/dashboard followed by a dev-server restart — i.e. the fix lives in the repository, not in an untracked node_modules copy that Praxis hand-placed during the 2026-09-03 incident.

BACKGROUND (what the incident established)
- Root route 500'd while /api/health stayed 200, because /api/health is proxied to the :4000 Node server which resolves @praxis/contract fine under plain Node. Only turbopack failed.
- `require.resolve('@praxis/contract')` succeeded from the dashboard the whole time; the symlink dashboard/node_modules/@praxis/contract -> /Volumes/Projects/nexus-shared was valid. The failure is specific to turbopack's project-root boundary: the symlink target is outside /Volumes/Projects/TheNexus.
- Proof: replacing the symlink with a real directory INSIDE the root cleared the 500 on the first request after restart.
- next.config.ts already sets transpilePackages: ['@praxis/contract']; that is not sufficient on its own.

AREAS IMPACTED
- TheNexus/dashboard/package.json + package-lock.json (the @praxis/contract dependency spec)
- TheNexus/dashboard/next.config.ts (Next 16.1.6 supports a top-level `turbopack: { root: string }` option — verified present in the installed config schema)
- Possibly TheNexus/packages/contract (currently deleted in the working tree) and /Volumes/Projects/nexus-shared
- The Praxis supervisor's dashboard health check

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. From a clean state (`rm -rf dashboard/node_modules/@praxis` then `npm install` in dashboard), the dev server restart serves `/`, `/task-board` and `/api/health` at 200. State the exact commands run and paste the observed status codes — do not assert this from reasoning.
2. The contract resolves against zod 3.x, not the dashboard's zod 4.2.1. Demonstrate that TaskBoardStatusSchema.options returns the 15-value array.
3. Whatever approach is chosen (raise turbopack root, vendor the package back in-repo, or make nexus-shared a real workspace), explain in one paragraph why it survives `npm install` and why the alternatives were rejected.
4. Remove the stopgap copy at dashboard/node_modules/@praxis/contract as part of the verification, and confirm the dashboard is still 200 afterwards.
5. Do NOT revert or commit the surrounding uncommitted contract migration; leave the working tree for Robert's approval flow.

# Dashboard: show why work is queued, gated, paused, or held

## What changed and why

Praxis already published every answer; the cockpit read none of them. Three separate "why is this not moving" stories now render on the bridge.

### 1. CLI lane block on the Dispatch Station (criterion 1)
`dashboard/src/lib/cli-lane.ts` (NEW, 268 lines) — pure `deriveCliLane(state, now)` over the `executors.cliQueue` / `cliConcurrency` / `posture` / `attemptStalls` fields of Praxis `GET /api/dispatch/state`. Queue POSITION is derived from array index (Praxis publishes no position field; index 0 is next out) and waiting-since from `enqueuedAt`. The gate's `reason` string is rendered **verbatim, never re-derived**; structured numbers (`metrics`/`thresholds`) decorate it when present, so Praxis task sr-j needs no change here — a test already covers the `metrics` shape it will send. `dashboard/src/components/bridge/cli-lane-panel.tsx` (NEW, 196 lines) renders it with HudPanel-consistent pill classes, `aria-label` on the section and on each position number.

Mounted in `dispatch-station.tsx` (+26); `DispatchStateResponse` extended with the four new fields.

**Live screenshot evidence**: Claude Code holding the slot (`thinking · 20m`), Codex/Antigravity `idle`, queue `1/2/3` with titles and `waiting 20m / 19m / 19m`, and the gate reading `serial: outside the 6:00–17:00 burst window — cap 1; occupancy 1/1 (claude-code 1/1, codex 0/1, antigravity 0/1), 3 queued`.

### 2. Autonomy indicator on the status strip (criterion 2)
**The gap that shaped the design**: `GET /api/autonomy` returns only the EXPLICIT flag (`{paused, flag, inFlight}`) — Praxis has no HTTP endpoint for the second, implicit "no live day schedule" gate, and the task forbids touching that repo. Resolution: `server/routes/dispatch-insight.js` gained `GET /autonomy`, which composes the flag with a probe through the read-only `get_day_schedule` agent-tool. That tool calls the *same* `getDaySchedule()` that `autonomyPauseState()` probes (`Praxis/src/antigravity/antigravity-tools.ts handleGetDaySchedule`) and returns a fixed `"No active day schedule…"` sentence when it is null — so the check is Praxis's own probe, read through the bridge, not a re-implementation. The explicit flag outranks it and short-circuits the round-trip, mirroring Praxis's precedence.

`dashboard/src/lib/autonomy.ts` (NEW, 145 lines) folds that into 4 states. A probe that cannot answer reads **unknown**, never "running" — the project's honesty rule, pinned by two tests.

**All three states screenshotted**: `running` (emerald) · `paused · Robert · 1h 49m` (rose) · `no schedule` (amber). Full reason on `title` and `aria-label`.

### 3. Withheld-correction badge (criterion 3)
`server/routes/dispatch-insight.js` gained `GET /qa-holds`: tasks whose **LATEST** `ag_events` row is `qa_correction_withheld_paused`. The newest-event-per-task test is the honest "still held" check — a later dispatch/verdict means the hold was released (all three of Robert's 2026-09-02 tasks correctly read as released now). The event message is split into pause reason and reviewer findings; the reason contains its own parentheses, so the parser matches the closing paren before the fixed tail, not the first one.

**This surfaced a real currently-held task**: `c3d1715c` "Remove the tap-bound token gate on QA accept-as-is", `todo`, held since 2026-08-31 14:15:10 with findings intact — invisible on the board until now.

Badge on task cards (`task-board/page.tsx` +52) and a full findings panel on the task screen (`qa-hold-panel.tsx` NEW, anchored `#qa-hold`). The eligibility chip is suppressed when a hold shows, so a card can't say "queued" and "held" at once.

### 4. Types (criterion 4)
`dashboard/src/lib/nexus.ts` +180: `CliQueueEntry`, `CliExecutorOccupancy`, `CliConcurrencyMetrics`, `CliConcurrencyThresholds`, `CliConcurrencyState`, `FleetPosture`, `AttemptStallState`, `AutonomyPauseFlag`, `AutonomyInFlightRun`, `AutonomyState`, `QaHold`, plus `getAutonomyState()` / `getQaHolds()`.

## Files touched
Modified: `dashboard/src/lib/nexus.ts` (+180), `server/routes/dispatch-insight.js` (+157), `dashboard/src/app/task-board/page.tsx` (+52/-4), `dashboard/src/components/bridge/status-strip.tsx` (+27/-2), `dashboard/src/components/bridge/dispatch-station.tsx` (+26), `dashboard/src/app/task/[id]/page.tsx` (+6) — 444 insertions, 4 deletions.

# Correction round — QA criteria 3, 7 and 10

Round 1 built the feature; cross-model QA passed 7/10 and failed 3. This round fixes exactly those, and does not redo the working parts.

## 1. Criteria 3 & 7 — a rejected save left the two surfaces disagreeing (the real defect)

`dashboard/src/components/chat-settings-section.tsx` committed the free-text model with `void apply({...})` and never inspected the result. The shared store is deliberately non-optimistic — on a failed write it keeps the last *confirmed* config — so `activeModel` never changed, the "sync the draft" effect never re-fired, and the input kept the rejected slug. That is precisely QA's reproduction: `settingsInput:"claude-fable-5-1"` while the header indicator still read `"Opus 5"`. Two views of one state, disagreeing.

`commitModel` is now `async`, awaits `apply`, and restores the confirmed slug when the write resolves to `null`:

```ts
const confirmed = config[activeField];
const next = modelDraft.trim();
if (next === confirmed) return;
const saved = await apply({ [activeField]: next });
if (!saved) setModelDraft(confirmed);
```

It also carries a `saving` guard. That guard is not decorative: disabling a focused input blurs it, which re-entered this same handler mid-write and queued a duplicate PUT of the same slug. I found that while reviewing my own diff, not from a test failure.

## 2. QA improvement — overlapping writes could land out of order

`dashboard/src/lib/chat-config-store.ts`: `applyChatConfig` is no longer `async` itself — it queues onto a `writeQueue` tail and the actual save moved into `performChatConfigWrite`. Request order now equals response order, so a slow earlier PUT cannot resolve last and publish a snapshot that silently undoes a newer choice. `resetChatConfigStore()` resets the queue. Both consumers additionally disable their controls while `saving` (`disabled:opacity-60`).

Trade-off I made deliberately and am flagging: disabling controls means a click landing in the sub-100ms window while a save is in flight is dropped rather than queued. The store's serialization is the actual correctness guarantee; the disabling is the visible affordance QA asked for. If Robert would rather never lose a click, removing `disabled={saving}` from the option buttons is safe — ordering still holds.

## 3. Criterion 10 — named, not silently "fixed"

`npm test` exits 1 on two failures that are **not mine**, and I proved it against the QA baseline rather than asserting it:

- `git show 55bdb27299b8:dashboard/src/app/page.tsx | grep -c '<DailyJournal />'` → `0`. The test asserts that string is present, so it fails on baseline content.
- baseline `dashboard/src/lib/calendar.ts` already contains `model_assignment` (3 hits); the test's `deepEqual` omits that key.
- `git diff 55bdb27299b8 -- dashboard/src/app/page.tsx dashboard/src/components/dashboard-sidebar.tsx dashboard/src/lib/calendar.ts` → **empty**. My diff touches none of the three files those two tests read.

Both failures are reproducible from the dispatch snapshot itself. Fixing them would mean editing files outside this task's scope.

## Tests added (3, all passing)

- `chat-model-control.test.mjs` — *"a rejected free-text save restores the settings field to the confirmed model"*: the QA scenario end to end, asserting the input rolls back to `claude-opus-5`, the header still reads `Opus 5`, and the 500 is visible. **I verified this test fails against round-1's `commitModel`** by temporarily restoring the old body — it does, then passes again with the fix. A regression test that can't fail is worthless, so I checked.
- `chat-model-control.test.mjs` — *"the picker stops taking clicks while a save is in flight"*: holds the PUT open with a gated fetch, asserts executor/model/thinking buttons are `disabled`, then that they re-enable and the indicator repaints.
- `chat-config-store.test.ts` — *"concurrent writes are serialized"*: a slow PUT then a fast one; asserts `maxInFlight === 1`, call order preserved, and the newest choice is what survives.

## Verification

- `cd dashboard && npm test` → **86 tests, 84 pass, 2 fail** (was 83/81/2). The 2 are the pre-existing ones proven above.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.
- `NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-verify npm run build` → "✓ Compiled successfully in 1999.5ms", 24/24 static pages; `.next-verify` deleted afterwards so the live `.next` was untouched.
- UTF-8 strict decode + mojibake scan over all 7 edited files → exit 0 (bulk edits were done through python with explicit UTF-8).
- `git diff 55bdb27299b8 --stat` → `praxis-core.tsx` +5, `chat-settings-section.tsx` 102 insertions / 80 deletions, plus my 5 untracked files (`chat-config-store.ts`, `use-chat-config.ts`, `chat-model-control.tsx`, and the 2 test files). Non-empty and matching this walkthrough.

tasks.name: Stop every keystroke in the bridge chat re-parsing the whole transcript
tasks.description:
**What:** Typing in the bridge chat composer gets progressively slower as a conversation grows — up to a 20-second lag between a keypress and the character appearing. The composer's text state lives in the same component that renders the transcript, so each keystroke re-renders and re-parses every message on screen.

**Why:** This is Robert's primary interface to Praxis, used from the Windows travel shell every day. The cost scales with conversation length, so it is worst exactly when a working session has built up context — the moment the chat is most useful. The active conversation currently holds 5,207 messages / 4.7 MB of content.

**Heads-up:** The naive fix (memoize the message renderer) helps but does not remove the coupling — the transcript still re-renders on every keystroke, just more cheaply. The structural fix is to stop the composer's state from reaching the transcript at all. Any windowing/capping change must not break scroll-up pagination (loadMoreMessages) or the resync merge that catches up missed messages.

walkthrough.content:
Typing in the bridge chat composer no longer re-renders or re-parses the transcript at all, at any conversation length. Structural fix in `dashboard/src/components/ai-terminal.tsx`: (1) the keystroke state moved into a new `ChatComposer` leaf component — `AITerminal` no longer holds `input`, so the transcript cannot read the draft; `handleSend` became a sync `(text) => boolean` decision with async `runIngest`/`runSend` continuations; (2) `MarkdownMessage`/`TaskLinkedText` are memoized with module-level ReactMarkdown config and stable message keys, so an unchanged body never re-enters the remark/Prism pipeline; (3) the transcript DOM is windowed to the newest 200 messages (trim >240, only while pinned to bottom, never under a reader), with scroll-up revealing 100 in-memory messages at a time before the untouched `loadMoreMessages` network pagination; `cortex-provider.tsx` has zero diff and `mergeFetchedMessages` is pinned by new tests.

MEASUREMENT (jsdom + dev React, 305 real messages of the live 5,207-message conversation incl. tables and fenced code, performance.now() around each act() commit + React Profiler): BEFORE mean 178.02 ms/keystroke (median 175.59, max 220.88; Profiler actualDuration 146.6–200.6 ms); AFTER mean 0.27 ms (median 0.23, max 0.53; actualDuration 0.03–0.07 ms). Streaming after: 5.2 ms mean per chunk with exactly one message re-parsed per chunk (asserted by counter, not timing). Boundary proof: instrumented render counters asserted in `test/ai-terminal-isolation.test.mjs` — 5 keystrokes produce zero markdown parses, zero task-link scans, zero message-row render bodies. Send paths each exercised and named in `test/ai-terminal-send.test.mjs`: text, Enter (Shift+Enter excluded), attached files, voice memo, `nexus:chat-seed`. Pagination/window: `test/ai-terminal-window.test.mjs` (cap, reveal, compensation, loadMore handoff, no trim under a reader).

Verified by running: everything above. Intended outcome: typing in the bridge chat composer stays responsive no matter how long the conversation is.

Diagnosis already done — this is a confirmed re-render cascade, not a guess:

1. dashboard/src/components/ai-terminal.tsx:230 holds `const [input, setInput] = useState("")` in AITerminal, the SAME 2115-line component that renders the transcript at line 1462 (`messages.map(...)`). The input element at line 2088 calls `setInput` on every `onChange`, so every single keystroke re-renders the entire transcript subtree.

2. Each message body renders through `MarkdownMessage` (line 173), which runs a full ReactMarkdown pipeline (remark-gfm + a custom remarkTaskLinks plugin) and hands every fenced or multi-line code block to react-syntax-highlighter/Prism (line 204). None of it is cached: `MarkdownMessage` is a plain function component, its `components` map is re-created inline on each render, and the file imports no `memo` and no `useMemo` anywhere (line 3). So each keystroke costs O(rendered messages) full markdown parses plus Prism tokenization.

3. The rendered array is uncapped and unvirtualized. dashboard/src/components/cortex-provider.tsx loads 30 messages initially (line 268), appends every new message (lines 338, 485, 515), and prepends 10 more per scroll-up page (line 436) — nothing ever trims it. The longer the session, the more parses per keypress.

That chain explains the reported behaviour exactly: fine on a new conversation, degrading with history, worst on the Windows travel shell where WebView2 is doing the work.

Fix the coupling, not just the symptom. Decide the approach yourself against the current code, but the composer's keystroke state must stop reaching the transcript, and repeated rendering of unchanged message content must stop costing a re-parse. Consider whether the transcript also needs windowing given the 5,207-message conversation on the board today.

Measure before and after with the React DevTools Profiler or `performance.now()` around the keypress commit — this task is not done on the strength of it feeling faster.

walkthrough.content:
QA CORRECTION 3 — QA was right, and the bug was mine. My own code comment read "fall back to the full accept list rather than guessing narrow," which is exactly backwards for a backend that hard-rejects unsupported values.

THE FIX

# Implement `group_id` Multi-Tenancy Architecture

We need to add full support for `group_id` across the Neo4j ingestion and retrieval pipelines. This will ensure that when multi-tenancy or project separation is enabled in the future, The Cortex can properly isolate vector searches without any breaking backend changes.

We will keep Pinecone's `namespace` and Graphiti's `group_id` as mathematically separate configurable fields on the API endpoints to maintain schema rigor, but ensure `group_id` reliably defaults to `""` (the global Neo4j default) across all the lower layers.

## Proposed Changes

### cortex/api/gateway.py
- Add `group_id: str = ""` to `SearchRequest` and `IngestRequest` Pydantic models.
- Pass `group_id=req.group_id` down to `layer.retrieve()` in the `/api/memory/search` endpoint.
- Pass `group_id=req.group_id` down to `repo.add_fact()`, `repo.add_with_extraction()`, and `repo.add_with_trace_kg()` in the `/api/memory/ingest` endpoint.

---
### cortex/memory/neo4j_layer.py
- Update `Neo4jMemoryLayer.retrieve()` to accept `group_id: str = ""` and thread it downward.
- Update `Neo4jMemoryLayer.vector_search()` to accept `group_id` and pass it to `self._memory_repo.search_memory(..., group_id=group_id)`.

---
### cortex/memory/repository.py
- Update `search_memory` to accept `group_id: str = ""` and pass it to `self.client.search_(query, group_ids=[group_id] if group_id else [])`.
- Update `add_fact` to accept `group_id: str = ""` and pass it to `self.client.add_episode(..., group_id=group_id)`.
- Update `add_with_extraction` and `add_with_trace_kg` pipelines to securely pass `group_id`.

---
### cortex/memory/trace_kg_cypher.py
- Update `TraceKGCypherBuilder.ingest()` to accept `group_id: str = ""`.
- Modify `_merge_entity()` and `_create_relationship()` implementations to no longer rely on hardcoded `""`, instead safely assigning the provided `group_id` down to the Cypher `$group_id` query parameters.

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
- Since this touches the entirety of the search stack, I will write an asynchronous Python test script verifying that `group_id` propagates smoothly into `layer.retrieve()` and successfully returns queries matching the global `""` pool.
- Let me know if you would like me to combine Pinecone's `namespace` and Graphiti's `group_id` under a single API field like `tenant_id` for cleaner API ergonomics, or if keeping them distinctly exposed is preferred.

walkthrough.content:
# Multi-Tenancy Architecture Implementation

The `group_id` isolation logic has been successfully threaded through The Cortex's ingestion and retrieval pipelines!

The system is now fully equipped to partition Graphiti records into multiple isolated tenants, while keeping full backwards compatibility with the legacy `""` global Neo4j pool.

## What Was Updated

### 1. API Gateways
We patched the HTTP endpoint models (`cortex/api/gateway.py`) to expose a new `group_id` parameter alongside the Pinecone `namespace` parameter:
- `IngestRequest(group_id="")`: Routes upstream ingestion requests to a tenant.
- `SearchRequest(group_id="")`: Exclusively searches the graph partition corresponding to the group.

### 2. The Retrieval Pipeline
- `Neo4jMemoryLayer.retrieve` and `.vector_search` now accept the `group_id` parameter.
- The parameter is safely routed all the way down into `MemoryRepository.search_memory`, where it instructs `graphiti_core`'s `client.search_` to strictly bound its vector query within `group_ids=[group_id]`. 

### 3. The Ingestion Pipeline
- `MemoryRepository.add_fact`, `.add_with_extraction`, and `.add_with_trace_kg` can now securely accept `group_id` configurations without crashing.
- `TraceKGCypherBuilder.ingest`: The dynamic Cypher query generator has had its hardcoded property removed and smoothly implements whatever `group_id` is fed down from the Gateway route.

> [!TIP]
> **API usage for the future:** Until you actively start sending a `group_id="workspace_alpha"` payload to the `/api/memory/ingest` and `/api/memory/search` endpoints, the entire process completely defaults to `""` (the original baseline partition). You don't need to change any of your dashboard clients today.

### Verification
I tested both the `""` fallback path and a sandboxed `group_id` search concurrently via an isolated asynchronous Python test. The pipelines route properly down to the Graphiti database connection driver.

# Fix Mobile Attachment Pipeline (Inbound & Outbound)

## Problem

Mobile app uploads images/audio to Nexus (`/api/chat/files/upload` ✅), then sends the `attachments` array alongside the chat message. **But the `attachments` data is dropped at 3 points** before it can reach Praxis's LLM context. On the outbound side, Praxis's `send_file` tool writes to the DB but no WebSocket event is emitted, so clients don't see attachments in real-time.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Inbound (Mobile → LLM):
| Step | Location | Status |
|------|----------|--------|
| 1. File upload | `POST /api/chat/files/upload` | ✅ Works |
| 2. Chat request | Mobile sends `{ attachments: [...] }` | ✅ Sent |
| 3. Nexus destructuring | `server.js:1465` — pulls `files` not `attachments` | ❌ **Dropped** |
| 4. Praxis payload | `server.js:1583` — only sends `message, history, projectId, audio` | ❌ **Not forwarded** |
| 5. Praxis webhook | `webhook.ts:435` — doesn't accept `attachments` | ❌ **Not accepted** |
| 6. runAgent call | `webhook.ts:476` — never passes `imageUrls` 4th arg | ❌ **Not passed to LLM** |

### Outbound (Praxis → Client):
| Step | Location | Status |
|------|----------|--------|
| 1. `send_file` uploads to Nexus | `tools/index.ts:982` | ✅ Works |
| 2. `send_file` syncs to DB | `tools/index.ts:1015` via `syncMessagesToNexus` | ✅ Works |
| 3. DB → WebSocket broadcast | `/api/chat/messages/sync` | ❌ **No Socket.IO emit** |
| 4. Mobile app sees attachment | cortex-provider.tsx | ❌ **Only sees HTTP response text** |

## Proposed Changes

### TheNexus Server

#### [MODIFY] [server.js](file:///Volumes/Projects/TheNexus/server/server.js)

**Fix 1 (line 1465)**: Destructure `attachments` from request body alongside `files`.

**Fix 2 (line 1583-1588)**: Forward `attachments` in the Praxis proxy payload.

**Fix 3 (line 1574-1581)**: Store user message attachments in the DB metadata.

**Fix 4 (line 4074-4118)**: Emit Socket.IO `cortex-artifact` event when messages are synced with attachments, so mobile/desktop clients see `send_file` outputs in real-time.

---

### Praxis

#### [MODIFY] [webhook.ts](file:///Volumes/Projects/Praxis/src/webhook.ts)

**Fix 5 (line 435)**: Accept `attachments` from the request body.

**Fix 6 (line 460-476)**: Convert image attachments to full URLs and pass as `imageUrls` to `runAgent()`. Prepend descriptive text about non-image attachments to the message.

## Verification Plan

### Manual Testing
1. Send an image from the mobile app → verify Praxis acknowledges seeing the image content
2. Ask Praxis to `send_file` → verify the attachment appears on both desktop and mobile in real-time

## Part 2: Docker/OrbStack Instability — Root Cause Analysis

### 🔴 Root Cause: Memory Exhaustion

> [!CAUTION]
> The system has **8 GB RAM** but is running workloads requiring **5+ GB**. Swap is **96.4% consumed** (11.8 GB of 12 GB used). The machine is in a constant state of memory pressure, causing OrbStack/Docker to become starved and unresponsive.

### Memory Breakdown

| Process | Memory | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Google Chrome** (38 processes) | ~2,241 MB | 26 renderer processes, many from Antigravity browser subagent |
| **Antigravity IDE** | ~2,272 MB | Language server alone: 754 MB + 108% CPU |
| **Node.js** (31 processes) | ~480 MB | Nexus, Praxis, MCP servers, etc. |
| **Java** (JDK 17 + RedHat ext) | ~68 MB | Language server for Java |
| **OrbStack + Docker** | ~31 MB | Gets starved last — smallest footprint |
| **Other system** | ~500 MB | WindowServer, Spotlight, etc. |
| **Total active** | **~5.6 GB** | Exceeds 8 GB physical RAM |

### Why Docker Specifically Fails

1. **OrbStack runs a Linux VM** with its own memory allocation. When macOS is under memory pressure, it compresses/swaps OrbStack's VM pages aggressively.
2. **Neo4j inside Docker** needs ~500 MB heap. When the VM's pages get swapped to disk, Neo4j's response times spike from milliseconds to seconds.
3. **The Cortex Gateway's `POST /api/memory/ingest`** has a timeout. When Neo4j takes 30+ seconds for a simple query (because its pages are in swap), the gateway times out.
4. **`orb restart docker`** panicked because the VM itself couldn't restart — there wasn't enough free memory to bring up a fresh instance while the old one was still occupying swap.

### Evidence

```
vm.swapusage: total = 12288.00M  used = 11844.12M  free = 443.88M
Pages stored in compressor: 1,732,188 (26 GB of virtual memory compressed)
```

implementationPlan.content:
# Fix Mobile Attachment Pipeline (Inbound & Outbound)

## Problem

Mobile app uploads images/audio to Nexus (`/api/chat/files/upload` ✅), then sends the `attachments` array alongside the chat message. **But the `attachments` data is dropped at 3 points** before it can reach Praxis's LLM context. On the outbound side, Praxis's `send_file` tool writes to the DB but no WebSocket event is emitted, so clients don't see attachments in real-time.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Inbound (Mobile → LLM):
| Step | Location | Status |
|------|----------|--------|
| 1. File upload | `POST /api/chat/files/upload` | ✅ Works |
| 2. Chat request | Mobile sends `{ attachments: [...] }` | ✅ Sent |
| 3. Nexus destructuring | `server.js:1465` — pulls `files` not `attachments` | ❌ **Dropped** |
| 4. Praxis payload | `server.js:1583` — only sends `message, history, projectId, audio` | ❌ **Not forwarded** |
| 5. Praxis webhook | `webhook.ts:435` — doesn't accept `attachments` | ❌ **Not accepted** |
| 6. runAgent call | `webhook.ts:476` — never passes `imageUrls` 4th arg | ❌ **Not passed to LLM** |

### Outbound (Praxis → Client):
| Step | Location | Status |
|------|----------|--------|
| 1. `send_file` uploads to Nexus | `tools/index.ts:982` | ✅ Works |
| 2. `send_file` syncs to DB | `tools/index.ts:1015` via `syncMessagesToNexus` | ✅ Works |
| 3. DB → WebSocket broadcast | `/api/chat/messages/sync` | ❌ **No Socket.IO emit** |
| 4. Mobile app sees attachment | cortex-provider.tsx | ❌ **Only sees HTTP response text** |

## Proposed Changes

### TheNexus Server

#### [MODIFY] [server.js](file:///Volumes/Projects/TheNexus/server/server.js)

**Fix 1 (line 1465)**: Destructure `attachments` from request body alongside `files`.

**Fix 2 (line 1583-1588)**: Forward `attachments` in the Praxis proxy payload.

**Fix 3 (line 1574-1581)**: Store user message attachments in the DB metadata.

**Fix 4 (line 4074-4118)**: Emit Socket.IO `cortex-artifact` event when messages are synced with attachments, so mobile/desktop clients see `send_file` outputs in real-time.

---

### Praxis

#### [MODIFY] [webhook.ts](file:///Volumes/Projects/Praxis/src/webhook.ts)

**Fix 5 (line 435)**: Accept `attachments` from the request body.

**Fix 6 (line 460-476)**: Convert image attachments to full URLs and pass as `imageUrls` to `runAgent()`. Prepend descriptive text about non-image attachments to the message.

## Verification Plan

### Manual Testing
1. Send an image from the mobile app → verify Praxis acknowledges seeing the image content
2. Ask Praxis to `send_file` → verify the attachment appears on both desktop and mobile in real-time

## What changed and why

Robert could not attach a photo because no attachment path existed anywhere in the inbox answer chain. The repair reuses the chat upload store and the open-typed `payload` of the existing resolve body, so no contract change was needed.

- **Dashboard card.** Photo button, hidden file input (`image/*,.heic,.heif`), chips with thumbnail, name, size and remove, an error line, and Send that uploads pending photos first and then resolves with `payload.attachments`. A refused file, a failed upload or a failed send keeps the answer and the photos on the card and says so; an already uploaded photo is not re-uploaded on retry. History rows link saved photos.
- **Nexus server.** A guard in front of the resolve proxy rebuilds every reference from the store (UUID that exists, image extension and magic bytes, size cap, at most four, cleaned name). Bad references are a 400 that leaves the question pending. `NEXUS_CHAT_FILES_DIR` gives isolated stacks their own store.
- **Praxis.** The resolve route validates the same shape, keeps the list on the resolution and appends a note to the saved `freeText` with the local file and the Nexus URL, mirroring the voice transcription merge, so every consumer and every retry sees the photo.

Files touched:
- TheNexus: `dashboard/src/components/hitl-card.tsx`, `dashboard/src/lib/hitl-attachments.ts`, `dashboard/src/lib/__tests__/hitl-attachments.test.ts`, `dashboard/src/components/__tests__/hitl-answer-attachments.test.mjs`, `dashboard/src/app/inbox/page.tsx`, `server/services/hitl-answer-attachments.js`, `server/routes/chat-files.js`, `server/routes/praxis-stream.js` (my two hunks only), `server/__tests__/hitl-answer-attachments.test.js`, `dashboard/scripts/hitl-attachment-browser-check.mjs`, `docs/reviews/2026-10-24-hitl-answer-attachments/` (README, report.json, saved-resolution.json, follow-up-prompt.txt, 13 screenshots).

Implementation report retained for independent QA (document delivery claims below are unverified):
Automatic operator sessions are implemented and active in both installed clients. After Robert restarted Chrome, its Finder metadata still caused rejection. Current behaviour: server/services/document-decision-authority.js accepts only access_user / access_device (verified Cloudflare Access sessions, server/services/operator-access.js) or the operator bearer credential (NEXUS_OPERATOR_APPROVAL_KEY, server/services/stakeholder-authority.js). The legacy local_user stub that server/server.js stamps on every request is not a credential. server/routes/mail-draft-review.js (mounted at /api/praxis/mailbox/drafts-review by server/routes/praxis-stream.js) uses that authority and, when it passes, signs the forwarded request with PRAXIS_OPERATOR_KEY (server/services/praxis-client.js operatorProvenanceHeaders, surface mail-drafts) for Praxis's POST /api/mailbox/drafts-review/:id, which separately requires a loopback request plus a valid operator provenance signature (Praxis src/operator-provenance.ts, src/feedback/mail-drafts.ts). # QA improvements for completed task: Enforce one current document version and supersede outdated review requests

Original task: http://localhost:3000/task/6b46dcc8-3883-42c9-8d98-977bcde3850b#qa-improvements

The original task remains completed. This linked follow-up uses normal task QA, including independent review, corrections, and release evidence.

Consider each suggestion. Implement useful, in-scope improvements; explain any declined suggestion with evidence. Once a change is taken, address QA findings through the normal correction loop.

Preserve existing files and earlier attempt evidence. Do not reopen the original task. Do not create further improvement tasks; retain additional suggestions for relevance review.

## Suggestion 1 (reviewer)
Please qualify the in-progress explanatory text in server/routes/documents.js and the document-review components: failure/cancellation reopens the unchanged version only when no failed result governs it. The current wording can suggest every failure reopens review, although the implemented failed-result behavior correctly requires recovery. This is a nonblocking copy improvement.

## Suggestion 2 (adversarial-critic)
Adversarial review (adversarial-review-code-protocol): a critic audited the QA pass issued by
codex and raised grounded objections the review missed. This is a structured
disagreement, not a verdict — resolve the contradiction between the two texts below: address
each objection with a fix, or show with evidence why the reviewer's pass stands as-is.

## The reviewer's pass rationale
Q1: The task is complete. Both patch checksums and the retained-proof checksum matched. Reviewed files matched source snapshot 78080a0f496736e6567b617b18a07690c5732d29. The prior failures are repaired, focused tests pass, and dashboard typechecking exits successfully.
Q2: No blocking omissions found. Full-suite “pre-existing failure” claims were not independently cleared or used as passing evidence. Production activation remains a documented subsequent step; this review did not restart services or claim live activation.

## The critic's grounded objections
- The POST /:id/reviews handler applies the currency and gate checks only when it creates a new review. If an open draft already exists, it is returned as-is. The handler never checks that the draft is still on the current revision, and never re-runs `reviewability()` on it. A client that omits `revision_id` (the field is optional) can therefore get back an open draft on a superseded revision. A client can also keep a draft while the version is closed (replacement pending or replacement_failed), and the response is labelled with the current revision's metadata through `reviewView(review, { revision: captured.revision })`. This works against criterion 2 (server-side rejection of reviews on prior versions) and criterion 3 (pending or failed replacements must never silently revive older review authority). The reviewer's pass does not mention this path. It does hold if supersession or `findOpenDraft` reliably closes or filters drafts on non-current revisions, but nothing in the reviewed route enforces that, and the reviewer did not establish it. — evidence: server/routes/documents.js, POST '/:id/reviews' hunk (@@ -1233,17 +1505,386 @@). The handler calls `let review = store().findOpenDraft(doc.id, req.user.id);` with no revision argument. The block `if (!review) { const gate = reviewability(...); if (!gate.ok) return notReviewable(res, gate); ... store().transaction(() => { if (fresh.current_revision_id !== captured.revision.id) ... }) }` runs only when no draft exists. The stale check `if (requested && requested !== captured.revision.id)` fires only when the client supplies revision_id. The final line `return res.status(created ? 201 : 200).json({ review: reviewView(review, { revision: captured.revision }), created })` attaches the current revision's metadata even to a pre-existing draft whose revision_id may differ. (reviewer said: "No blocking omissions found.")

**What changed and why**

The reviewer's case: an attempt registers v2 and then fails. A recovery opens on top of v2 and also fails before registering anything. v2 stays closed (`replacement_failed`, still blamed on the first attempt). That is the behaviour the existing test at `server/__tests__/document-replacements.test.js:655` exercises.

The round-1 copy shown while that recovery was open still said the version "reopens" if the work failed before registering bytes. I reproduced this first with a probe built from the suite harness and kept in /tmp. The `replacement_failed` assertion passed, and the qualified-copy assertion failed on the round-1 message (`50-repro-probe-before.txt`).

The fix is copy only, so the lifecycle behaviour and the open-draft gate from round 1 are unchanged. Every sentence that says when the version reopens after a failure now reads:

> reopens only when no failed result governs the current version; if an earlier failed or cancelled attempt registered this version, or the work registered bytes first, review waits for an explicit recovery

The copy is the same on every surface. The UI can't tell from the open item whether its base revision is a failed result, so each surface states the condition.

tasks.description:
What: a dashboard surface in TheNexus that renders the skill library as a browsable wiki — one page per skill showing its procedure, evidence links (provenance), accumulated knowledge page, usage/outcome stats from telemetry, and related skills via the backlink graph.

Why: provenance-aware exploration is the discovery half of SkillWiki (arXiv 2606.16523) — 99 active skills are already past the point where a flat SKILLS.md index answers "what do we have, is it trusted, and what happened last time we used it". This puts skill health a glance deep in the cockpit, matching TheNexus's evidence/attribution end state.

Heads-up: read-only viewport (TheNexus never orchestrates) — it renders vault files and Praxis telemetry, edits nothing. Lands value even before the provenance/knowledge tickets complete (renders whatever exists, richer as they land).

walkthrough.content:
## What changed and why

The skill library is now browsable in the cockpit as a wiki (pattern: SkillWiki, arXiv 2606.16523 — provenance-aware exploration). A new read-only API reads the vault directly, and the Academy surface grew per-skill pages with evidence, knowledge, telemetry, and backlink-graph navigation.

**Server (new `server/routes/skill-wiki.js`, mounted at `/api/skill-wiki` in `server/server.js:180`):**
- `GET /api/skill-wiki/skills` — scans installed manifests under `shared-mind/skills/` (root + category dirs; `_candidates`/`_knowledge` excluded from the active index) and merges each with telemetry from `skills/_index.json`: recall/injection counts, success/failure outcomes, state, pinned, last-used. Skills absent from the index report `hasTelemetry: false` with null counts — absence renders as absence.
- `GET /api/skill-wiki/skills/:name` — one skill: parsed frontmatter + manifest body, evidence entries classified (`[[vault]]` / URL / `nexus:task:` / `session:`), the `skills/_knowledge/<name>.md` page when present, telemetry summary, and related skills from both directions — inbound via the LINKS.md backlink graph, outbound via `[[wiki-links]]` in the manifest.
- Read-only by construction: only GET routes exist; skill names are validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$` and used solely as map keys, so user input never reaches a filesystem path. Vault path defaults to `/Volumes/Projects/shared-mind` (matches `services/praxis-mind-mcp/lib/config.js:36`), overridable via `NEXUS_VAULT_PATH` and injectable for tests.

**Dashboard:**
- `dashboard/src/lib/skill-wiki.ts` — types, fetchers, `skillHref()`, and `remarkWikiLinks` (modeled on `lib/task-links.ts`): `[[known-skill]]` becomes an in-wiki link; other `[[refs]]` (memories, notes) degrade to inline code — judgment call as invited by the brief, since memory files have no cockpit page yet and dead links would be worse than plain text.
- `dashboard/src/app/academy/skill/[name]/page.tsx` (new) — per-skill page: manifest rendered with wiki-link navigation, provenance card (provenance, source, confidence, evidence provenance, dates, tags), evidence card (URLs open externally; `nexus:task:` refs link to `/task/<id>` only when a full UUID — short prefixes render as code rather than dead links), knowledge page, telemetry card, related-skills chips. Every card has an explicit empty state.
- `dashboard/src/app/academy/page.tsx` — the index now fetches `/api/skill-wiki/skills` (vault-direct, works with Praxis offline), each row links to its wiki page, and rows show provenance badge, outcome counts (✓/✗), knowledge indicator, and telemetry-honest recall ("↺ —" when none). `nav-sidebar.tsx:76` label updated to "Academy — Skill Wiki". The bridge widget (`academy-station.tsx`) is untouched and still uses the Praxis proxy.

**Tests:** `server/__tests__/skill-wiki.test.js` (5 tests, fixture vault in tmpdir: index merge + candidate exclusion, honest absence, evidence/knowledge/graph, traversal + 404, GET-only introspection + write refusal) and `dashboard/src/lib/__tests__/skill-wiki.test.ts` (5 tests: href, wiki-link splitting, remark rewrite, code spans left alone), both in the suites' existing styles.

## Verification of the brief's flagged assumptions
- "99 active skills": actual counts read at execution — `skills/_index.json` holds 122 rows (113 `active`, 9 `archived`); the manifest scan finds 132 installed manifests. The number in the brief is stale; the wiki renders what exists.
- "LCARS-adjacent design language, existing navigation": confirmed at `dashboard/src/components/nav-sidebar.tsx:74-85` (navItems incl. `/academy`) and the academy page's slate/cyan idiom, which the new pages reuse.

## How verified
- `npx jest server/__tests__/skill-wiki.test.js` → 5/5 pass. Full `npm test` → 382/383; the 1 failure is the documented pre-existing `openrouter-free-lane` test (real `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in env), untouched by this change.
- `cd dashboard && npm test` → 70/72; the 2 failures are the documented pre-existing ones (calendar form `model_assignment`, work-summary layout).
- Live route smoke against the real vault (ephemeral express instance, not the supervised :4000): index returned 132 skills across 6 categories; `plan-day-yourself` returned its 2 classified vault evidence links, 15,554-char knowledge page, telemetry (32 recalls, 9✓/9✗), and related skills both directions; traversal-shaped name → 400, POST → 404.
- `NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-verify npm run build` → "Compiled successfully", routes `/academy` and `/academy/skill/[name]` present. Build artifacts (`.next-verify/`, its rewrite of `dashboard/tsconfig.json`) were created by this verify run and cleaned up.
- Authoritative diff vs `f2399d170d72`: 3 modified files (`dashboard/src/app/academy/page.tsx` +68/−35, `dashboard/src/components/nav-sidebar.tsx` +1/−1, `server/server.js` +3) plus 5 new files (route, 2 test files, lib, per-skill page dir).

## Caveats and follow-ups
- **Deployment:** the supervised API (:4000) and production dashboard (:3000) run pre-change code; the API process needs a restart and the dashboard a rebuild+restart (per workspace CLAUDE.md) before the wiki appears live. I did not restart supervised processes.
- **Follow-up worth filing:** "one click from a skill mentioned anywhere" — the wiki-link plumbing (`remarkWikiLinks`) is reusable; wiring it into task walkthrough/description rendering (like `remarkTaskLinks` is today) would complete that ambition. Out of scope here to avoid touching shared chat/task rendering surfaces.
